{{short description|German mathematician}}
[[File:Herbert Spohn.jpg|thumb|220px|Spohn at [[Oberwolfach]], 2010]]
'''Herbert Spohn''' (born 1 November 1946) is a German mathematician and mathematical physicist working in kinetic equations, dynamics of stochastic particle systems, hydrodynamic limit, kinetics of growth processes, disordered systems, open quantum systems, dynamics of charged particles coupled to their radiation field, Schrödinger operators, functional integration and stochastic analysis.

His PhD was obtained in 1975 at [[LMU Munich]] under the supervision of {{ill|Georg Süßmann|de}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.genealogy.ams.org/id.php?id=77111|title = Herbert Spohn – the Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref>

He is currently (in the year 2021) [[:wikt:emeritus|Emeritus]] Professor of the [[TUM Department of Mathematics|Department of Mathematics]] of the [[Technical University of Munich]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Herbert Spohn - Department of Mathematics - TUM |url=https://www.math.cit.tum.de/math/personen/professuren/spohn-herbert/ |access-date=2026-05-01 |website=Department of Mathematics |language=de}}</ref><ref>[https://www.emeriti-of-excellence.tum.de/a-z/herbert-spohn Emeritus], TUM Emeritus of Excellence, retrieved 24 January 2019.</ref>

He obtained several prizes. In 2011, he was awarded the [[Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics]],<ref>[http://www.research-in-germany.de/58194/2011-01-03-prof-herbert-spohn-awarded-dannie-heineman-prize-for-mathematical-physics-2011,sourcePageId=8240.html Prof. Herbert Spohn awarded Dannie Heineman Prize for Mathematical Physics 2011] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726155342/http://www.research-in-germany.de/58194/2011-01-03-prof-herbert-spohn-awarded-dannie-heineman-prize-for-mathematical-physics-2011,sourcePageId=8240.html |date=26 July 2011 }}, Research in Germany, retrieved 13 March 2012.</ref> the Leonard Eisenbud Prize for Mathematics and Physics (AMS) and the Premio Caterina Tomassoni e Felice Pietro Chisesi Prize of University of Roma
"La Sapienza". He is Docteur Honoris Causa de L'Université Paris-Dauphine. In 2017, he
received the [[Max Planck Medal]] of the [[German Physical Society]], in 2019, the
[[Boltzmann Medal]] of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]].

He wrote the books ''Large Scale Dynamics of Interacting Particles'' (Springer, 1991)<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Rost | first1 = Hermann | year = 1993 | title = Review of ''Large Scale Dynamics of Interacting Particles'' | journal = Journal of Statistical Physics | volume = 73 | issue = 3–4| pages = 803–806 | doi = 10.1007/BF01054353 | s2cid = 123237709 }}</ref> and ''Dynamics of Charged Particles and Their Radiation Field'' (Cambridge University Press, 2004).

He gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited talk at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010, on the topic of "Mathematical Physics".<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=15 August 2013|archive-date=8 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Spohn is the brother of the historical sociologist {{ill|Willfried Spohn|de}} and of the analytic philosopher [[Wolfgang Spohn]].

Together with [[Michael Prähofer]] he introduced the [[Airy process]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Michael|last1=Prähofer|first2=Herbert|last2=Spohn |title=Scale Invariance of the PNG Droplet and the Airy Process |journal=Journal of Statistical Physics|publisher=Springer |volume=108 |date=2002 |issue=5/6 |pages=1071–1106 |doi=10.1023/A:1019791415147 |arxiv=math/0105240|s2cid=11701694 }}</ref>
